posts.author: Cherry
posts.body:
There is a "Help" button in almost every window, it has a lot of useful info!
It says width 288, height 256, and 4x2 characters in one file.
Yours is not that format. You have only one, and your size is probably 72x128.
Also, it appears your image is in 24-bit color format, not 8-bit. The same help page says this:
Extend the image to be 288x256 so it looks like the other charsets already existing and make sure it is in 8-bit color format, then it will work!
Like this:
Also, I'd recommend using a different title than "HELP ME" next time. It should summarize what your issue is about, for example here "Invalid Image Size error when importing charset" would work.

posts.author: DevRPG2k
posts.body:
This happens when you edit any image in MSPaint on Windows 10 and 11 when importing. At least that's what I found in my tests, I use Paint.NET to change the background color with a paint bucket or by creating a new layer.
But if you use a dedicated Pixel Art editor like Aseprite or its alternative Libresprite, you can easily see the image's color palette and remove colors without actually having to click pixel by pixel.

posts.author: Cherry
posts.body:
Invisnir said:
i'm using piskel for this, and normally when its all zero its black, not green.
you know the color number for it?
Click to expand...
The number does not the define the actual color of the color, if that makes sense. 8-bit color means you have 256 colors, but you can choose what color each color has (damn, it's hard to put this in words).
So if you use, say, red and green and blue as your only three color, your palette would be:
0 = red
1 = green
2 = blue
3-255 = doesn't matter
Then every pixel that has the color index 2 would be blue because you assigned blue on the palette index 2. In this example however, the red would become transparent in most places in the RPG Maker game because index 0 would be used for transparency.
If you import the image and then click some color area during the import, RPG Maker will swap that palette entry with the one on position 0 so that now the selected one becomes index 0, i.e. transparent.
